sources.title: Les fonds territoriaux: Afrique occidentale française
sources.usage: Body read: AOF administrative/archive paragraph identifies Governor-General and Guinea, Niger and Senegal colonial governments. Federation founded 1895; listed territories are not all assumed members from that first day.

sources.title: Before independence: constitutional history
sources.usage: Body read: Chronological body: 1874 governor and councils, Accra seat 19 March 1877; 1895 nominated institutions, 1925 elective representation, 1946 reserved governor powers, 1951 Assembly, 1952 premiership and 1954 cabinet reform. Obvious 1866 Lagos and 1877/1887 heading/date inconsistencies not adopted.

sources.institution: Senegal Ministry of Culture and Tourism; Iba Der Thiam and Mbaye Guèye
sources.title: Histoire du Sénégal
sources.usage: Body read: Historical sections describe colonial coastal enclaves, inland resistance, expansion from 1876, AOF from 1895, Saint-Louis colonial capital until 1957 and governors/cercle hierarchy. Postwar electoral and independence shorthand not used.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: Guinea: recognition and diplomatic relations
sources.usage: Body read: Recognition body: Republic recognized 1 November 1958; earlier French West Africa; embassy 13 February 1959. Recognition is not independence date.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: FRUS 1958–1960 XIV, Document 330: 6 October 1960 conversation
sources.usage: Body read: Participant list and conversation body attest President Sekou Touré and Guinean ministers on 6 October 1960. One-day role record, no inferred whole tenure.

sources.institution: US Department of State, Office of the Historian
sources.title: Niger: recognition and diplomatic relations
sources.usage: Body read: Republic recognition/diplomatic relations on independence 3 August 1960; message to Prime Minister Hamani Diori; embassy established 3 February 1961. PM attestation not extended across later constitutional changes.

sources.title: Kaarta: Dizionario di Storia (2010)
sources.usage: Body read: Complete short body identifies distinct Bambara kingdom, separation from Segu, regained independence and late eighteenth-century rulers, later nineteenth-century conquest. Nioro not assumed capital in 1800; conflicting 1854/1855 conquest precision omitted.

sources.title: Segu: Dizionario di Storia (2011)
sources.usage: Body read: Complete short body identifies Bambara kingdom, eighteenth-century dynasties and Sikoro. Erroneous/imprecise claim of entire Segu conquest in 1818 is excluded; only the early-1800 kingdom framework curated.

sources.institution: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division (public chapter mirror)
sources.title: Nigeria: Usman dan Fodio and the Sokoto Caliphate
sources.usage: Body read: Full historical chapter: jihad 1804, Hausa kingdoms overthrown by 1808 with exceptions, Sokoto founded 1809; loose confederation of emirates under caliph; Borno not conquered. Usman death 1817 does not warrant uninterrupted practical personal government.

sources.title: The Fulani Empire of Sokoto: H. A. S. Johnston, Oxford University Press, 1967
sources.usage: Body read: Repository item body, title, author/date/publisher and description independently establish scholarly name Fulani Empire of Sokoto. Book contents not represented as read; dated institutions use LoC chapter.

sources.institution: International Court of Justice repository; Republic of Niger party pleading
sources.title: Counter-Memorial of Niger: contested Dendi historical authority
sources.usage: Body read: Pleading body §§1.5–1.9 and 1.32–1.35 distinguishes Dendi region/language/groups and contests Benin claims of unified Karimama authority. This is an interested litigant statement, not a Court historical finding. No unified Dendi government invented.

sources.title: Sarmento Rodrigues: Governador da Guiné (1945–1949)
sources.usage: Body read: Archive description gives governor 15 March 1945–20 January 1949; installation subrecord is May 1945. Editorial coverage begins June, after installation, and ends before January 1949 handover.

sources.title: Les résistances à la colonisation française en Afrique noire (1871–1914), Africa Development XVIII/4 (1993)
sources.usage: Body read: PDF body pp123–124: first realm and professional army in 1881–1882; Almamy title from 1886, eastern retreat after January 1892, later realm and capture September 1898. No theocratic label projected backward or beyond failed homogenization.

sources.institution: Bibliothèque nationale de France, Centre national de littérature pour la jeunesse
sources.title: Samory: Farouche combattant, critical notice
sources.usage: Body read: Review body explicitly associates Samory Touré with Wassoulou/Mandingue empire; reviewer flags epic narrative and unspecified context. Used only for conventional name association, never precise chronology or institutions.

sources.institution: Institut de recherche pour le développement; Cogneau, Mesplé-Somps and Spielvogel
sources.title: Development at the border: national integration in post-colonial West Africa (2010), appendix A.2–A.3
sources.usage: Body read: PDF appendix pp46–49 explicitly distinguishes first western realm and second empire attested in 1896. Scholar-sourced historical text, not map-derived identity; modern coordinate/locality details and succession links excluded.

sources.institution: The National Archives, United Kingdom; Keith Mitchell
sources.title: Cataloguing West African records (21 November 2025)
sources.usage: Body read: Historical body: German Togo surrendered August 1914, divided 1916; British Cameroon administered from Nigeria; Northern/Southern mandates identified; catalogued records 1914–1926. Formal mandates distinguished from legal sovereignty and later UN trusteeship.

sources.title: First World War: East Africa teachers’ notes
sources.usage: Body read: PDF background p1 dates Togoland capture 26 August 1914; German colonies and British/French wartime campaign context. Capture not interpreted as formal annexation.

sources.title: The Southern Cameroons (Constitution) Order in Council 1960, SI 1960/1654
sources.usage: Body read: Primary legal body: effective 1 October 1960; Crown-appointed Commissioner, elected House and ministers; clauses32–40 reserve Commissioner powers, Premier appointment and Executive Council. Internal government not full independence.
